cover_headline: Foreign Investors Pump ₹84,290 Crore Into Indian Stocks in November's First Fortnight
facts: Foreign portfolio investors put a net ₹84,290 crore into Indian equities between November 2 and 13, reversing two straight months of outflows
FPIs had withdrawn ₹34,843 crore in October and ₹35,861 crore in September, and cumulative outflows for 2026 narrowed to about ₹2.1 lakh crore
Brent crude fell about 13% in the first week of November to nearly $97 a barrel, and financials, telecom and pharmaceuticals led the buying

end.headline: Foreign Investors Pump ₹84,290 Crore Into Indian Stocks in November's First Fortnight
end.line: After pulling ₹70,704 crore out in September and October, FPIs returned in nine straight sessions — but strategists call the turn tactical, not structural.

quote.text: November's foreign buying is a sharp tactical turn, not yet a structural return.
quote.speaker: Vedant Gupte
